faqs.q: What is a Barcelona coupling with female thread used for?
faqs.a: A Barcelona coupling with female thread is an aluminium claw-type water coupling half that screws onto a male pipe thread, linking a hose to fixed pipework, a tap or a pump port. Barcelona is the Spanish fire-service and irrigation pattern, used on hydrant and pump lines and agricultural water distribution.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Barcelona female-thread coupling come in?
faqs.a: It is listed from 3/4" to 4" in aluminium with an NBR gasket. The Barcelona pattern is made in aluminium for weight on the larger irrigation and fire sizes; state the size and thread type when you enquire.

faqs.q: What does a Barcelona female-thread coupling connect to?
faqs.a: It mates with another Barcelona half, with the claws pushed together and given a quarter turn against the NBR gasket. It will not connect to a Geka or GOST coupling, because the patterns only fit themselves; see [GOST, Barcelona and Geka couplings](/blog/gost-barcelona-and-geka-couplings).

faqs.q: Barcelona or Geka coupling: which pattern do I need?
faqs.a: Barcelona is the Spanish fire and irrigation standard in aluminium from 3/4" to 4", while the German Geka pattern is in brass from 1/4" to 1" (see the [Geka female-thread coupling](/p/geka-coupling-with-female-thread)). They do not connect to one another, so match the pattern already on your hose or hydrant.

faqs.q: What are Barcelona couplings made of and how do they seal?
faqs.a: The body is aluminium and the seal is an NBR gasket. The gasket does the sealing, so a joint that weeps is almost always a perished or missing gasket rather than a worn claw; replace it before replacing the coupling.

faqs.q: What is the pressure rating of the Barcelona female-thread coupling?
faqs.a: The listing does not publish a working pressure for the Barcelona coupling, so we do not quote one. Give us the pressure, the medium and the size and we confirm the rating with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: How do you connect and disconnect a Barcelona claw coupling?
faqs.a: Push the two halves together and give a quarter turn so the claws lock against the NBR gasket; no tools are needed. Check the gasket seat is clean and the gasket is present before each connection.

faqs.q: Where are Barcelona couplings used?
faqs.a: Barcelona couplings are used on fire-service hydrant and pump lines and across agricultural irrigation in Spanish-influenced markets. Both Barcelona and Geka are specified where a connection has to be made by hand, repeatedly, without tools.

faqs.q: Does the Barcelona female-thread coupling carry any approvals?
faqs.a: The listing carries no standards or approvals for the coupling, so we do not claim any. If you need a fire-service approval or a test report, ask for it with the enquiry and we request it from the maker.

faqs.q: What thread does the Barcelona female-thread coupling have?
faqs.a: It has a female thread to screw onto a male pipe end; the thread standard and pitch are not published in the listing. Send us the pipe thread you have, for example BSP or NPT, and we confirm the right variant before you order.

faqs.q: What is a Geka cap used for?
faqs.a: A Geka cap is a brass blanking cap for a Geka claw coupling, closing a line that is out of service. It fits the Geka half in 1/4" to 1", seals on an NBR gasket and fits with a quarter-turn twist.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Geka cap come in?
faqs.a: It is listed from 1/4" to 1" in brass with an NBR gasket. Name the size of the Geka coupling it will close when you enquire.

faqs.q: Which Geka couplings does the Geka cap fit?
faqs.a: It fits the Geka halves in the same size, such as the [Geka hose shank coupling](/p/geka-coupling-hose-shank) and the male-thread and female-thread halves. It will not fit a Barcelona or GOST coupling; see [GOST, Barcelona and Geka couplings](/blog/gost-barcelona-and-geka-couplings).

faqs.q: What is the Geka cap made of?
faqs.a: The cap is brass with an NBR gasket. Brass tolerates potable and mildly aggressive water, which is why Geka is made in brass rather than aluminium.

faqs.q: Can a chain be fitted to a Geka cap?
faqs.a: Yes. The maker notes that chains can be attached upon request, so the cap stays with the coupling and is not lost. State this on the enquiry with the size.

faqs.q: Geka cap or Geka male-thread coupling: which one closes a line?
faqs.a: A Geka cap blanks a line by closing a Geka half, while the [male-thread coupling](/p/geka-coupling-with-male-thread) connects a Geka line to a female pipe or tap. Use the cap on an unused coupling and the threaded half to make a connection.

faqs.q: What pressure is a Geka cap rated for?
faqs.a: The listing publishes no pressure rating for the Geka cap, so we do not quote one. Give us the line pressure and the size and we confirm it with the maker; the NBR gasket does the sealing.

faqs.q: Where are Geka couplings used?
faqs.a: Geka is the German utility-water pattern found on garden and washdown hose, small pumps, compressors and general site water in continental Europe. Caps blank the unused end.

faqs.q: Does the Geka cap meet any standard?
faqs.a: The listing carries no standards or approvals for the Geka cap, so we do not claim any. Geka is a German utility pattern; ask us for the maker's documents if your project needs more.

faqs.q: How do you fit and remove a Geka cap?
faqs.a: Push the cap onto the Geka half and give a quarter turn so the claws lock against the NBR gasket; reverse to remove. Check the gasket is present and not perished before each use.

faqs.q: Can the Geka cap be exported from Dubai?

faqs.q: What is a Geka hose shank coupling used for?
faqs.a: A Geka hose shank coupling is a brass claw-type water coupling half with a multi-serrated hose tail, for joining a hose to another Geka half. It is the German utility-water pattern used on washdown hose, garden hose, small pumps and compressors.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Geka hose shank coupling come in?
faqs.a: It is listed from 1/4" to 1" in brass with an NBR gasket, with a multi-serrated tail for the hose. Give the hose bore so the matching shank size is supplied.

faqs.q: What is a multi-serrated hose shank on a Geka coupling?
faqs.a: A multi-serrated shank has several ridges along the tail so the hose grips it and the clamp holds. The maker notes that this Geka coupling has a multi-serrated hose shank; fit it with a hose clamp, see [hose clamps, sleeves and ferrules](/c/hose-clamps-sleeves-ferrules).

faqs.q: What does a Geka hose shank coupling connect to?
faqs.a: It mates with another Geka half by a quarter-turn claw lock against the NBR gasket, such as the [male-thread half](/p/geka-coupling-with-male-thread). It will not connect to Barcelona or GOST couplings; see [GOST, Barcelona and Geka couplings](/blog/gost-barcelona-and-geka-couplings).

faqs.q: Geka hose shank coupling or Geka female-thread coupling: what is the difference?
faqs.a: The hose shank half takes a hose on its tail, while the [female-thread half](/p/geka-coupling-with-female-thread) screws onto a male pipe or tap. Use the shank to terminate a hose and the threaded half to tie into fixed pipework.

faqs.q: What is the pressure rating of the Geka hose shank coupling?
faqs.a: The listing publishes no pressure rating for the Geka hose shank coupling, so we do not quote one. Give us the working pressure and the hose and we confirm it with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: How do you assemble a Geka hose shank coupling to a hose?
faqs.a: Push the hose fully over the serrated shank and fit a clamp over the serrations. Then connect to the mating Geka half with a quarter turn; a leak at the joint is usually the NBR gasket.

faqs.q: Where is a Geka hose shank coupling used?
faqs.a: Geka is used on garden and washdown hose, small pumps, compressors and general site water in continental Europe. It is specified where connections are made by hand, repeatedly, without tools.

faqs.q: Does the Geka hose shank coupling carry any standard or approval?
faqs.a: The listing carries no approvals for this coupling, so we do not claim any. Brass tolerates potable water in practice, but ask us for the maker's documents if you need a drinking-water approval.

faqs.q: What hose does a Geka hose shank coupling take?
faqs.a: The shank is made for hose of the same nominal bore, from 1/4" to 1"; the listing does not publish the shank outside diameter, so give us the hose bore and wall and we confirm the fit before you order.

faqs.a: A Geka coupling with female thread is a brass claw-type half that screws onto a male pipe thread, tying a Geka hose line into fixed pipework, a tap or a pump port. It is the German utility-water pattern in 1/4" to 1".

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Geka female-thread coupling come in?
faqs.a: It is listed from 1/4" to 1" in brass with an NBR gasket. Give the pipe thread size and type so the correct female thread is supplied.

faqs.q: What does a Geka female-thread coupling connect to?
faqs.a: On one side it screws onto a male thread; on the other it mates with a Geka half such as the [hose shank coupling](/p/geka-coupling-hose-shank) by a quarter-turn twist. It does not connect to Barcelona or GOST patterns.

faqs.q: What is the Geka female-thread coupling made of?
faqs.a: The body is brass and the gasket is NBR. Brass tolerates potable and mildly aggressive water; the gasket is the part that wears, so keep spares.

faqs.q: Geka female-thread or male-thread coupling: which do I need?
faqs.a: Use the female thread where the pipe or tap has a male thread, and the [male-thread half](/p/geka-coupling-with-male-thread) where the pipe has a female port. The Geka claw side is the same on both.

faqs.q: What pressure is the Geka female-thread coupling rated for?
faqs.a: The listing publishes no pressure rating for it, so we do not quote one. Give us the working pressure and size and we confirm it with the maker before you order.

faqs.q: How do you install a Geka female-thread coupling on a pipe?
faqs.a: Seal the male thread with a suitable sealant, tighten the body by its flats and check the NBR gasket sits correctly before connecting. A weeping claw joint is usually a perished gasket.

faqs.q: Where are Geka female-thread couplings used?
faqs.a: They tie hose lines to fixed pipework on washdown stations, small pumps, compressors and general site water in continental Europe. Pair them with Geka hose shank halves for the hose side.
